title: Watermark Backpressure Bisect Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to capture commands, observations, and cheap repros for the intermittent "slow-first-chunk / chunking stalls" bug observed in streaming (SSE) endpoints. Goal: produce a tiny, repeatable local repro and a clear hypothesis to validate with tracing and kernel captures.

Summary of the issue (symptoms):
- Client receives first few bytes quickly then long stall (~3-30s) before subsequent chunks.
- Stalls coincide with bursts of concurrent requests or when payloads cause large KV-cache growth on the worker.
- Affected flow: hosted-api streaming (text-generation) -> runtime writer thread -> tokio/h2 send queue -> client.

Observed on: dev/staging clusters and occasionally in production (low freq).
Recent occurrence: 2026-02-10 14:12 UTC (staging) during load test 300rps.

Commands I used to reproduce locally: (run from mac/linux devbox)
1) Simple SSE curl streaming (baseline):
   curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/streaming?model=gpt-small \
     -d '{"prompt":"say hi\n\nrepeat 200 times","max_tokens":500}'

2) Python requests streaming (makes it clearer how client reads):
   python3 - <<PY
import requests
url = 'https://localhost:8080/v1/stream'
p = {'model':'gpt-small','prompt':'repeat me ' * 100}
with requests.post(url, json=p, stream=True, verify=False) as r:
    for i, chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=None)):
        print(f'CHUNK {i} len={len(chunk)}')
        if i > 10: break
PY

3) Local repro that induces backpressure by creating many active KV caches:
   - start 6 local workers (small memory) pinned to one GPU (or emu mode)
   - run 150 concurrent short streams (hey.py script) that use long context (~8k tokens) to inflate KV cache
   - watch sendq with: sudo ss -ti | grep ESTAB -A3 and dstat for CPU/IO

4) Simulate packet delays to amplify stalls (Linux tc):
   sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms 50ms distribution normal
   (then run curl streaming test)

Representative error snippets / logs seen:
- client: "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" then first SSE payload, then nothing for 12s, then a cluster of chunks.
- client debug: "read timeout waiting for next frame after 12012 ms"
- worker logs: "sendq short-circuit: backlog 1052 > soft_limit 1000, marking conn throttled"
- runtime: "writer stalled waiting for writable -> waking after 12041ms"
- k8s node syslog: "socket sendmsg EAGAIN (would block) for pid 27413"
- nginx proxy: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" (rare)

Captured metrics (staging run):
- per-request: first-chunk latency p50 80ms, p95 320ms; subsequent-chunk inter-arrival p50 40ms, p95 15s (tail)
- worker metrics: sendq_len spikes to ~1500, evictions ~120/min during incident
- kernel tcp: tcp_wmem/writesockq increased; backlog drops shown in /proc/net/sockstat

Hypotheses (ordered for quick validation):
1) Client-side slow-read + server edge: clients stop reading for a few seconds (due to GC, thread scheduling), OS socket send buffer fills -> sendmsg returns EAGAIN -> server writer sleeps -> multiple requests cause queueing and storms.
   - Quick test: run client consumer that aggressively reads into /dev/null (cat) and see if stalls persist.
2) Runtime writer/coalescing logic: when KV cache grows (large context), the runtime produces big first frames and then switches to smaller deltas. Writer uses a single mutex + NIO write path; under contention it blocks and OS buffer backlog increases.
   - Quick test: instrument writer lock hold times and add metrics around bytes_written_per_call.
3) Proxy (nginx/edge) interplay: an upstream change to sendbuffer or keepalive_time interacts with sparse writes causing head-of-line stalls.
   - Quick test: bypass proxy (direct to worker) to see difference.
4) TCP layer interaction: delayed ACKs combined with Nagle for small packets cause coalescing => bursts after ACKs. Manifest when server does many small writes.
   - Quick test: disable Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) in runtime and re-run repro.
5) Epoll/event-loop starvation in node/python client when many streams opened concurrently causing observed client pause (less likely given server logs show EAGAIN).

What I tried & results:
- Reproduced locally by creating 120 concurrent streams with long prompt -> saw sendq_len > 1000 and repeated "EAGAIN" in worker logs. (repro success)
- Disabled Nagle on runtime side (temporary toggle) -> reduced magnitude of bursts but didn't eliminate stalls.
- Bypassed nginx (direct to runtime) -> stalls still present but nginx-only timeouts disappeared.
- Increased OS send buffer sizes (sysctl net.core.wmem_max) -> reduced EAGAIN frequency but still observed tail stalls.
- Added short write-yield in writer loop (sleep 0) to let epoll progress -> reduced global latency under load but still saw some per-connection stalls.

Cheap tracing to capture next:
- Add per-connection chronology: timestamps at (a) request receive, (b) first write call, (c) sendmsg return, (d) kernel EAGAIN events (via strace -e sendto), (e) last write.
- strace against worker: strace -f -e trace=sendto -p <pid> -> capture frequency of EAGAIN, blocking syscalls.
- tcpdump on node loopback to watch packet timing and bursts: sudo tcpdump -i lo tcp port 8080 -w capture.pcap
- run perf top on writer thread to ensure not CPU-starved.

Minimal repro plan (local):
1) start single worker in debug mode with small send buffer (SO_SNDBUF=32k) and tcp_nodelay toggles
2) spawn N clients with python script that pauses after first chunk for X seconds (to mimic slow reader) and record server logs.
3) toggle Nagle and OS buffer sizes to validate TCP hypothesis.
4) instrument writer lock hold and bytes-per-write with counters exposed via /metrics.

Sample one-liner to spawn 60 slow readers (Linux):
for i in $(seq 1 60); do 
  (curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"lorem"}' | head -c 20; sleep 10; cat) &
done

Quick notes about differences from previous tickets:
- Unlike the "frame-drop" bugs, here the TLS/handshake is fine; we see normal 200 + initial payload. It's the inter-chunk timing and repeated EAGAIN on worker send.
- Also differs from pure client-timeout reports because server logs show backlog/EAGAIN not just client timeouts.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Add lightweight tracing in writer: record timestamps for each write call and bytes_written. Push as a flagged build to staging. (priority: high)
- Run local minimal repro above on my laptop with strace/tcpdump to confirm EAGAIN pattern (priority: med)
- Create a tiny kernel-level test to prove delayed-ACK/Nagle hypothesis (priority: low)
- If confirmed, plan mitigations: increase send-buffer, break big writes into controlled smaller writes + yield, or rate-limit per-connection KV growth.

Notes to collaborators:
- Liam: see linked PR (repro-cases #412) for a small harness I started. I added a toggle for TCP_NODELAY.
- Marco: if you have a quick way to dump per-socket sndbuf backpressure metrics in prod, that would be extremely helpful.

Unresolved questions:
- Why do some workers handle load without hitting EAGAIN while others escalate quickly? (suspect NUMA/CPU pinning or different kernel settings)
- Is there any runtime-level buffercoalesce code that could re-order writes leading to clumps?

Housekeeping: saved artifacts:
- pcap captures: /tmp/wmb-pcap-20260218.pcap
- worker strace dump: /tmp/wmb-strace-20260218.txt
- local harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-cases/tree/main/watermark-backpressure

If I don't get to the tracing this week, next good checkpoint is: produce 1-min strace + tcpdump that shows repeated sendto EAGAIN then succeeding bursts, attach to INC-2026-0312.

-- end --
